title: The managed block rcf init writes states the twelve rules, and rcf doctor upgrades a 0.40.1 block in place

acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] Given the installed pack, when `rcf guidance managed/agent-instructions-block` runs, then it exits 0 and prints RULE 13 headed "RULE 13: Deliver in rounds: the twelve rules", its section holding the twelve rules as one list numbered 1 to 12 in order: rule 1 the chain refereed by `rcf define validate` and `rcf audit coverage --strict`; rule 2 criteria only for promises, the rest hygiene tests; rule 3 the proof level (full, journey or external) chosen at DEFINE and recorded with the round, every touched criterion still needing a bound test and a Code Node (ruling R0 E1); rule 4 the five stages DEFINE, BUILD, REVIEW, TEST, FINALISE in order; rule 5 separation verbatim ("The hand that writes production code never writes or edits a criterion-bound test, a binding or criterion text. The audit enforces this by path on every commit, and the merge check runs the audit."); rule 6 red-first verbatim ("From the named base-suite record, only the newly added or changed test cases fail at the DEFINE head, and each fails at its recorded assertion; an unrecorded baseline failure makes DEFINE BLOCKED.", with no throwaway); rule 7 the BUILD exit; rule 8 REVIEW, with no sentence that test strength is recorded for the reviewer's adequacy verdict; rule 9 TEST; rule 10 FINALISE writing complete; rule 11 the round budget of two DEFINE passes; rule 12 spec readiness. In the Build loop, REVIEW runs `rcf audit test-strength` read-only, with no `--record`, and TEST runs `rcf audit test-strength --record`. The block contains none of "How to talk to your operator", "at most ONE question", "The method's failure modes are yours to catch", "Each stage is done by its own role", "optional through 0.37.x", "the suite fails on exactly the new tests"; RULE 1 to 12 and 14 to 17 keep their 0.40.1 headings.

[happy] Given a fresh empty directory, when `rcf init` runs there, then it exits 0 and the text between the managed markers of CLAUDE.md (and of AGENTS.md where it writes one) is exactly the block `rcf guidance managed/agent-instructions-block` prints, the block of AC-20503-1.

[happy] Given a project whose CLAUDE.md carries, between project text of its own, the managed block the 0.40.1 `rcf init` wrote, when `rcf doctor` runs, then it exits 3 naming the stale agent-instructions block in CLAUDE.md; when `rcf doctor --fix` runs, then it exits 0 and rewrites only the text between the markers, to the block of AC-20503-1, the text above and below the markers byte-identical; and a second `rcf doctor` exits 0.

[must-not] Given a project whose CLAUDE.md carries a stale managed block whose end marker is followed by a CRLF line ending, or by the end of the file, when `rcf doctor --fix` runs, then it exits 2, names CLAUDE.md, and writes nothing: the file stays byte-identical, so no rewrite changes a byte outside the markers.
